newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak PM Meciar says interest rates too high.
newsitem.headline: Slovak PM Meciar says interest rates too high.

text.p: Slovak Prime Minister Vladimir Meciar on Tuesday said rates on the domestic interbank market were artificially high and that the government had begun talks with banks to see them move lower.
"Interbank rates have moved up on a one-sided surge, the banks are keeping them artificialy high to increase their profits," Meciar told parliament during question hour.
"We have already been in negotiations with banking circles and have agreed to solve this problem," he said adding he expected rates to fall in the near future.
Money market rates ranged on Thursday between around 22 percent on overnight money and 18 percent for six-month funds.
Interbank rates jumped to record levels in the first weeks of January after the NBS moved to rein in a rapidly growing money supply and cool off a consumption-led boom.

The latest NBS move to hold securities repurchase tenders instead of quoting repo rates -- which many domestic banks often used to refinance their activities -- brought an acute liquidity shortage on the interbank market at the beginning of the year, pushing rates to around 27 percent.

Last week Finance Minister Sergej Kozlik sharply criticised the central bank's restrictive monetary policy, saying it could hurt the entire economy. He said NBS attempts to rapidly reduce money supply growth were inappropriate.
